clue.text: Nearly all this paper's a flop? It'll be a blast in due course

definitions.text: It'll be a blast in due course

indicators.note: nearly all means the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the clue appears in The Times, so this paper is the Times
a bomb is a theatrical or commercial flop

explanation.surface: A gloomy reader wonders if the whole newspaper is a failure, then ends with a cryptic warning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly all' trims TIMES (the newspaper the clue is printed in) to TIME; BOMB is the failure.
explanation.definitionFit: A device set to explode at a later moment is literally a blast waiting to happen.

clue.text: Having a guide, also getting taken round Spanish city

indicators.note: one piece has another wrapped around it, so these words signal a container

parts.note: also means too
someone with a guide is led

explanation.surface: A tourist joins a guided tour of a Spanish city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting taken round' tells you the word for also wraps around the word for guided.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic city in central Spain, famous for its swords.

clue.text: Going to other places of sentimental significance

definitions.meaning: travelling or relocating is a sense of the participle

explanation.definitionFit: The participle means relocating, and as an adjective it means emotionally touching.

clue.text: One showing pressure, more open about old police?

indicators.note: about means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: barer means more exposed or open
the Met is the Metropolitan Police of London

explanation.surface: A question about whether the old police force was more transparent.
explanation.walkthrough: BARER is placed about O and MET; the Met is London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: A barometer is the instrument that measures and displays atmospheric pressure.

clue.text: Just over half glimpse S America represented in this style of art?

indicators.note: represented suggests the letters are presented again in a new order
glimpse has seven letters, so just over half is its first four

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A painter catches a brief glimpse of South America and depicts it in a particular artistic style.
explanation.walkthrough: GLIM (four of the seven letters of glimpse) plus SAMERICA are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a literary and artistic genre, strongly linked with South American writers, that blends the fantastic with the everyday.

clue.text: One, when in bed, is favouring a particular idea

indicators.note: in means these pieces go inside the other one

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

explanation.surface: Someone lying in bed holds a partisan view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts the numeral and the word for when inside the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being prejudiced means leaning towards one view rather than judging fairly.

clue.text: One's never following the score at billiards?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
no can mean not ever, as in 'no more'
ff is the abbreviation for following pages

explanation.surface: A billiards player complains that he is never next to score.
explanation.walkthrough: In billiards an in-off is a shot where the cue ball goes into a pocket off another ball, which scores points.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards the in-off is a scoring stroke where the cue ball is pocketed after striking another ball.

clue.text: Piano — a couple of ways to secure one for Beethoven

indicators.note: to secure means the outer pieces hold the inner one fast

parts.note: ST is an abbreviation for street, one kind of way
a way is a road or path
Beethoven was German, and German for one is ein

explanation.surface: A musician finds two methods to get a piano for playing Beethoven.
explanation.walkthrough: The two ways are ST and WAY; together they hold EIN, the German word for one.
explanation.definitionFit: Steinway is a famous maker of concert pianos, so the name stands for the instrument.

clue.text: Girl's expression of horror embraced by escort, runs

indicators.note: something embraced is held inside, so this signals a container

parts.note: a date is a companion for an evening out
ugh is an exclamation of disgust
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A girl shrieks in horror when her escort takes her hand and she flees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraced by' sets the exclamation inside the companion; runs is cricket shorthand.
explanation.definitionFit: A daughter is a girl in relation to her parents.

clue.text: Almost even temper is an advantage

indicators.note: almost means the word stops one letter short

parts.note: level means even or flat
rage is a fit of temper

explanation.surface: Keeping a nearly even temper is said to help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Almost' drops the final letter of the word for even.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is a position of advantage or power over someone.

clue.text: Island doctor has additional gold

parts.note: more means extra or additional
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A doctor on an island has piled up yet more gold.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Moreau is the scientist of H G Wells's novel The Island of Doctor Moreau.
explanation.definitionFit: In Wells's novel the title character is a scientist on a remote island.

clue.text: Party's aim: to restrict source of writing

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance party
the point is the aim or purpose
to pen is to confine or shut in

explanation.surface: A political party's goal is to censor what gets written.
explanation.walkthrough: A charade of BALL, POINT and PEN.
explanation.definitionFit: This common pen is literally the tool the writing comes from.

clue.text: Day this writer's returning — material

indicators.note: returning means the word is read backwards

parts.note: this writer is the setter, me, so this writer's is mine

explanation.surface: A writer gets back the day's fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns the possessive word for this writer's backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Denim is a hard-wearing cotton twill fabric used for jeans.

clue.text: Bird rejected 'bits of corn in church

parts.note: chaff is the husks of corn thrown away after threshing

explanation.surface: A bird turns its beak up at pieces of corn inside a church.
explanation.walkthrough: A charade of CHAFF, IN and CH.
explanation.definitionFit: A chaffinch is a common European finch.

clue.text: A couple of points to be observed, if it's an amateur cross-country?

definitions.text: A couple of points to be observed, if it's an amateur cross-country?

parts.words: A couple of points to be observed, if it's an amateur cross-country?
parts.note: the old amateur cross-country race was run between two church spires, the pointed landmarks riders kept in sight

explanation.walkthrough: The race got its name from riders racing across country towards a distant church spire as their landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: The horse race over obstacles began as a cross-country race between church spires.

clue.text: London location for team from lower division?

definitions.meaning: a street in the City of London
a side from a lower league is cheaply assembled, read cryptically as a low-cost team

explanation.walkthrough: Cheapside is a historic street in the City of London; read as two words it suggests a low-budget team.
explanation.definitionFit: The London street name splits into an adjective for low-cost and a word for a team.

clue.text: Was successful installing central heating, getting burnt

indicators.note: installing means putting one piece inside another

parts.note: scored means achieved a success

explanation.surface: A heating engineer did well fitting a boiler but got burned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'installing' fits the heating abbreviation inside the word for succeeded.
explanation.definitionFit: Scorched means burnt on the surface by heat.

clue.text: Ancients appearing decrepit, for example

indicators.note: decrepit means broken down, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Old people look worn out, to give a case in point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appearing decrepit' rearranges ANCIENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a single case or illustration of something.

clue.text: Where people keep an eye on stacks of crates?

definitions.text: Where people keep an eye on stacks of crates?

parts.words: Where people keep an eye on stacks of crates?
parts.note: crates is slang for old aircraft and stacks are planes circling in layers waiting to land, all watched from the airport building

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a warehouse, but 'crates' is slang for aircraft and a stack is planes queuing in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Air traffic controllers watch aircraft from the tall airport building.

clue.text: Slight item apparent between raisin and sultana?

indicators.note: an item visible at the tail of the first fruit word supplies its closing letters
between the two fruits, so the second word gives its opening letters next

explanation.surface: Something unimportant seen among dried fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters straddle raisIN and SULTana, skipping the link word 'and'; the question mark flags this loose hiding.
explanation.definitionFit: A slight is a snub or insult.

clue.text: Question trapping university's would-be know-all

indicators.note: trapping means holding the other piece inside

parts.note: a poser is a puzzling question
U is the abbreviation for university

explanation.surface: A tricky question catches out a university's self-styled expert.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside POSER.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseur pretends to knowledge or sophistication he or she does not have.

clue.text: A portion's spread out — to kill?

definitions.note: read as 'something to kill', a noun idea

indicators.note: spread out means the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A serving is laid out, with murderous intent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spread out' rearranges APORTIONS; the definition reads as 'something to kill with'.
explanation.definitionFit: Rat poison is a substance laid down for killing rodents.

clue.text: .Deferred skating?

definitions.meaning: on a frozen surface, playfully read

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means postponed, and literally describes a skater on frozen water.

clue.text: Recalled work involving soldier, a theatrical work

indicators.note: involving means taking the other piece inside
recalled suggests calling back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
an ant is a soldier, as in soldier ants

explanation.surface: A remembered production with a soldier in it was a stage show.
explanation.walkthrough: OP backwards gives PO, which takes in ANT. Panto, short for pantomime, is a British Christmas comic stage show.
explanation.definitionFit: Panto is the British family stage entertainment staged at Christmas.

clue.text: Some fibrous stuff — that is, a type of rag

parts.note: a hank is a coil of yarn or thread
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: Some woolly material, namely a kind of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: A charade of HANK and IE.
explanation.definitionFit: A handkerchief is a small square of cloth, a rag for the nose.

clue.text: Skill? Update it with retraining

indicators.note: retraining reshapes things, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A manager says skills can be refreshed by training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with retraining' rearranges UPDATEIT.
explanation.definitionFit: An aptitude is a natural ability or talent.

clue.text: Stops US railroad engine

parts.note: an engine that stops dies
the El is an elevated railway in American cities such as Chicago

explanation.surface: An American train engine stalls.
explanation.walkthrough: A charade of DIES and EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is a locomotive or engine running on diesel fuel.

clue.text: Person with idea has opening in iron smelting

indicators.note: in means this piece goes inside the other
smelting melts ore down, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: a vent is an opening

explanation.surface: Someone has a bright idea about an opening in an iron furnace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smelting' rearranges the metal to INOR; 'in' puts the opening inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who devises something new starts with an idea.
